title: BRUCK SYNDROME 2
alt_titles: OSTEOGENESIS IMPERFECTA WITH CONGENITAL JOINT CONTRACTURES

intro.text: A number sign (#) is used with this entry because of evidence that Bruck syndrome-2 (BRKS2) is caused by homozygous mutation in the PLOD2 gene (601865) on chromosome 3q24.

checks.claim: Bruck syndrome-2 (BRKS2) is caused by homozygous mutation in the PLOD2 gene.
checks.evidence_quote: he was shown to be homozygous for a novel mutation leading to an Arg598His substitution in PLOD2
checks.explanation: BS type 2 is defined as caused by PLOD2 mutations; patient homozygous.

checks.claim: The PLOD2 gene is located on chromosome 3q24.
checks.evidence_quote: two mutations in the lysyl hydroxylase 2 gene (PLOD2, 3q23-q24) have been identified in BS
checks.explanation: Paper gives 3q23-q24, not specifically 3q24.

paragraphs.text: Bruck syndrome is an autosomal recessive disorder in which features of osteogenesis imperfecta, including bone fragility with multiple fractures, occur together with congenital contractures of the large joints (Ha-Vinh et al., 2004). The underlying defect is in hydroxylation of lysine residues in the telopeptides of collagen (Ha-Vinh et al., 2004), which leads to abnormal collagen crosslinking in bone (Bank et al., 1999).

checks.claim: Bruck syndrome is an autosomal recessive disorder.
checks.evidence_quote: Bruck syndrome (BS) is a recessively-inherited phenotypic disorder
checks.explanation: Recessive inheritance stated.

checks.claim: In Bruck syndrome, features of osteogenesis imperfecta, including bone fragility with multiple fractures, occur together with congenital contractures of the large joints.
checks.evidence_quote: featuring the unusual combination of skeletal changes resembling osteogenesis imperfecta (OI) with congenital contractures of the large joints
checks.explanation: Matches the description.

checks.claim: The underlying defect in Bruck syndrome is in hydroxylation of lysine residues in the telopeptides of collagen.
checks.evidence_quote: there is biochemical evidence for a defect in the hydroxylation of lysine residues in collagen 1 telopeptides
checks.explanation: Stated directly.

checks.claim: The defect in telopeptide lysine hydroxylation in Bruck syndrome leads to abnormal collagen crosslinking in bone.
checks.evidence_quote: We report that lysine residues within the telopeptides of collagen type I in bone are underhydroxylated, leading to aberrant crosslinking
checks.explanation: The abstract says underhydroxylation of telopeptide lysines in bone leads to aberrant crosslinking.

paragraphs.text: Bank et al. (1999) found underhydroxylation of the lysine residues in collagen telopeptides in bone from patients with Bruck syndrome. This caused abnormal collagen crosslinking in bone, whereas crosslinking in ligament and cartilage was normal. They suggested that a bone-specific telopeptide lysyl hydroxylase was deficient.

checks.claim: Bone from patients with Bruck syndrome showed underhydroxylation of lysine residues in collagen telopeptides.
checks.evidence_quote: We report that lysine residues within the telopeptides of collagen type I in bone are underhydroxylated
checks.explanation: The abstract directly states that telopeptide lysines in bone are underhydroxylated in Bruck syndrome.

checks.claim: Underhydroxylation of telopeptide lysine residues caused abnormal collagen crosslinking in bone from patients with Bruck syndrome.
checks.evidence_quote: lysine residues within the telopeptides of collagen type I in bone are underhydroxylated, leading to aberrant crosslinking
checks.explanation: The abstract states that the underhydroxylation leads to aberrant crosslinking in bone.

checks.claim: Collagen crosslinking in ligament and cartilage from patients with Bruck syndrome was normal.
checks.evidence_quote: In contrast to bone, cartilage and ligament show unaltered telopeptide hydroxylation as evidenced by normal patterns of crosslinking.
checks.explanation: The abstract reports normal crosslinking patterns in cartilage and ligament.

checks.claim: Bank et al. (1999) suggested that a bone-specific telopeptide lysyl hydroxylase was deficient in Bruck syndrome.
checks.evidence_quote: this might be the BS (Bruck syndrome) locus and consequently the region where bone telopeptidyl lysyl hydroxylase is located
checks.explanation: The title ('indications for a bone-specific telopeptide lysyl hydroxylase on chromosome 17') and the abstract propose that a bone-specific telopeptide lysyl hydroxylase is the defective enzyme in Bruck syndrome.

paragraphs.text: Bruck syndrome is inherited in an autosomal recessive pattern (Ha-Vinh et al., 2004). The patient reported by Ha-Vinh et al. (2004) was homozygous for a PLOD2 mutation. Puig-Hervás et al. (2012) studied 6 consanguineous families with Bruck syndrome, in all of which they found mutations in either PLOD2 or FKBP10.

checks.claim: Bruck syndrome is inherited in an autosomal recessive pattern.
checks.evidence_quote: Bruck syndrome (BS) is a recessively-inherited phenotypic disorder
checks.explanation: Recessive inheritance stated.

checks.claim: The Bruck syndrome patient reported by Ha-Vinh et al. (2004) was homozygous for a PLOD2 mutation.
checks.evidence_quote: he was shown to be homozygous for a novel mutation leading to an Arg598His substitution in PLOD2
checks.explanation: Stated directly.

checks.claim: Puig-Hervás et al. (2012) studied 6 consanguineous families with Bruck syndrome.
checks.evidence_quote: Herein, we sought mutations in six consanguineous BS families and detected changes in either PLOD2 or FKBP10 in all cases.
checks.explanation: The abstract states that the study looked at six consanguineous Bruck syndrome families.

checks.claim: In all 6 consanguineous Bruck syndrome families studied by Puig-Hervás et al. (2012), mutations were found in either PLOD2 or FKBP10.
checks.evidence_quote: Herein, we sought mutations in six consanguineous BS families and detected changes in either PLOD2 or FKBP10 in all cases.
checks.explanation: The abstract states that changes in PLOD2 or FKBP10 were found in all six families.

paragraphs.text: Bruck syndrome is genetically heterogeneous (Ha-Vinh et al., 2004). Bruck syndrome-1 (BRKS1) maps to chromosome 17p12 (Ha-Vinh et al., 2004) and is caused by mutation in the FKBP10 gene (Puig-Hervás et al., 2012). Bruck syndrome-2 is caused by mutation in the PLOD2 gene (Ha-Vinh et al., 2004), which van der Slot et al. (2003) identified as a putative telopeptide lysyl hydroxylase gene.

checks.claim: Bruck syndrome is genetically heterogeneous.
checks.evidence_quote: two mutations in the lysyl hydroxylase 2 gene (PLOD2, 3q23-q24) have been identified in BS, showing genetic heterogeneity
checks.explanation: Stated directly.

checks.claim: Bruck syndrome-1 (BRKS1) maps to chromosome 17p12.
checks.evidence_quote: One BS locus has been mapped at 17p12
checks.explanation: Stated directly (abstract later says 17p22 for BS type 1, apparently a typo).

checks.claim: Bruck syndrome-1 (BRKS1) is caused by mutation in the FKBP10 gene.
checks.evidence_quote: PLOD2 and FKBP10 are genes mutated in Bruck syndrome (BS), a condition resembling osteogenesis imperfecta (OI), but that is also typically associated with congenital joint contractures.
checks.explanation: The abstract says FKBP10 is mutated in Bruck syndrome and that FKBP10 changes were found in some families. It does not name a Bruck syndrome-1 / BRKS1 subtype.

checks.claim: Bruck syndrome-2 is caused by mutation in the PLOD2 gene.
checks.evidence_quote: caused by mutations in PLOD2 (BS type 2)
checks.explanation: Stated directly.

checks.claim: van der Slot et al. (2003) identified PLOD2 as a putative telopeptide lysyl hydroxylase gene.
checks.evidence_quote: we found two missense mutations in exon 17 of PLOD2, thereby identifying PLOD2 as a putative TLH gene
checks.explanation: The abstract says this directly. TLH is defined in the abstract as telopeptide lysyl hydroxylase.

paragraphs.text: In patients with Bruck syndrome, van der Slot et al. (2003) found 2 missense mutations in exon 17 of the PLOD2 gene. This identified PLOD2 as a putative telopeptide lysyl hydroxylase gene.

checks.claim: van der Slot et al. (2003) found 2 missense mutations in exon 17 of the PLOD2 gene in patients with Bruck syndrome.
checks.evidence_quote: By analyzing the genetic defect of Bruck syndrome, which is characterized by a pyridinoline deficiency in bone collagen, we found two missense mutations in exon 17 of PLOD2
checks.explanation: The abstract states this directly.

checks.claim: The finding of PLOD2 missense mutations in Bruck syndrome patients identified PLOD2 as a putative telopeptide lysyl hydroxylase gene.
checks.evidence_quote: we found two missense mutations in exon 17 of PLOD2, thereby identifying PLOD2 as a putative TLH gene
checks.explanation: The abstract states this directly.

paragraphs.text: Ha-Vinh et al. (2004) reported a boy with Bruck syndrome who had congenital contractures with pterygia at birth, along with severe osteogenesis imperfecta-like osteopenia and multiple fractures. He was homozygous for a mutation in the PLOD2 gene.

checks.claim: Ha-Vinh et al. (2004) reported a boy with Bruck syndrome.
checks.evidence_quote: We report on a boy who had congenital contractures with pterygia at birth
checks.explanation: Boy with BS reported.

checks.claim: The boy with Bruck syndrome reported by Ha-Vinh et al. (2004) had congenital contractures with pterygia at birth.
checks.evidence_quote: We report on a boy who had congenital contractures with pterygia at birth
checks.explanation: Stated directly.

checks.claim: The boy with Bruck syndrome reported by Ha-Vinh et al. (2004) had severe osteogenesis imperfecta-like osteopenia.
checks.evidence_quote: severe OI-like osteopenia and multiple fractures
checks.explanation: Stated directly.

checks.claim: The boy with Bruck syndrome reported by Ha-Vinh et al. (2004) had multiple fractures.
checks.evidence_quote: severe OI-like osteopenia and multiple fractures
checks.explanation: Stated directly.

checks.claim: The boy with Bruck syndrome reported by Ha-Vinh et al. (2004) was homozygous for a mutation in the PLOD2 gene.
checks.evidence_quote: he was shown to be homozygous for a novel mutation leading to an Arg598His substitution in PLOD2
checks.explanation: Stated directly.

paragraphs.text: Puig-Hervás et al. (2012) identified PLOD2 mutations in additional patients with Bruck syndrome. They also found PLOD2 mutations in patients with autosomal recessive osteogenesis imperfecta (AR-OI), including one with mild AR-OI. They concluded that PLOD2, in addition to causing Bruck syndrome, is also associated with AR-OI phenotypes of variable severity, which widened the phenotypic spectrum.

checks.claim: Puig-Hervás et al. (2012) identified PLOD2 mutations in additional patients with Bruck syndrome.
checks.evidence_quote: Two probands were found with a homozygous frameshift mutation in the alternative exon 13a of PLOD2, indicating that specific inactivation of the longer protein isoform encoded by this gene is sufficient to cause BS.
checks.explanation: The abstract reports PLOD2 mutations in Bruck syndrome probands, and also in a brother with mild Bruck syndrome.

checks.claim: Puig-Hervás et al. (2012) found PLOD2 mutations in patients with autosomal recessive osteogenesis imperfecta (AR-OI).
checks.evidence_quote: we identified a homozygous donor splice site mutation in PLOD2 in a patient with autosomal-recessive OI (AR-OI). Screening of additional samples also revealed compound heterozygous mutations in PLOD2 in two brothers, one affected with mild AR-OI
checks.explanation: The abstract reports PLOD2 mutations in two patients with AR-OI.

checks.claim: One of the patients with AR-OI who had a PLOD2 mutation in the study by Puig-Hervás et al. (2012) had mild AR-OI.
checks.evidence_quote: compound heterozygous mutations in PLOD2 in two brothers, one affected with mild AR-OI and the other with mild BS
checks.explanation: The abstract states that one of the brothers had mild AR-OI.

checks.claim: Puig-Hervás et al. (2012) concluded that PLOD2, in addition to causing Bruck syndrome, is associated with AR-OI phenotypes of variable severity.
checks.evidence_quote: Thus, PLOD2 in addition to causing BS is also associated with AR-OI phenotypes of variable severity.
checks.explanation: The abstract states this conclusion directly.

checks.claim: Puig-Hervás et al. (2012) concluded that the association of PLOD2 with AR-OI widened the phenotypic spectrum of PLOD2 mutations.
checks.evidence_quote: Thus, PLOD2 in addition to causing BS is also associated with AR-OI phenotypes of variable severity.
checks.explanation: The abstract says PLOD2 is associated with AR-OI as well as Bruck syndrome, and the title places these disorders on a BS–OI spectrum. It never says the spectrum was widened; that wording is the draft's interpretation.
